<details><summary>AI feedback</summary>

Proposed fixes for defects D1 and D2 aren't applied yet.

D1: When `update document for history step application` reuses an existing `navigation`'s `activation` on BFCache reactivation (for example, cross-origin or non-contiguous same-origin BFCache restoration where `previousEntryIndex` is negative and `navigationType` is `"traverse"` rather than `"replace"`), missing an `Otherwise` branch leaves `activation`'s `old entry` (`navigation.activation.from`) set to its prior value instead of `null`.
Not applied: [proposed fix (spec)](https://github.com/noamr/html/commit/57fea33), [proposed fix (test)](https://github.com/noamr/wpt/commit/185516d)

D2: No WPT checks `navigation.activation === savedActivation` across BFCache reactivation, and `navigation_committed.py` only tests initial `<iframe src>` loading during a top-level navigation rather than navigating an existing child iframe directly.
Not applied: [proposed fix](https://github.com/noamr/wpt/commit/cac67cd)

<details><summary>Reviewed commits</summary>

Reviewed at 8252a15 on 0e292f4, with web-platform-tests/wpt@90d3906, using spec-pr-review.
</details>
</details>

Thanks, Noam. I added the fallback that clears `navigation.activation.from` when the previous entry is not exposed. https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/65675 adds coverage for same-origin BFCache activation reuse and for the BiDi `navigationCommitted` event when an existing child iframe is navigated directly. I haven’t completed a full browser run locally.

@noamr I have strengthened the cross-origin regression test in https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/65675 by starting from the existing same-origin seed document and requiring a non-null initial `activation.from`. The test then checks reuse of the saved activation object and clearing of that old entry after BFCache restoration. This prevents an already-null entry from satisfying the clearing assertion.

On 4265f43, Chrome passes both BFCache cases and all 21 BiDi cases, including 10 stability repetitions. Firefox passes the cross-origin BFCache case and all 21 BiDi cases; the same-origin case reports a null activation before traversal. Safari fails both BFCache cases at saved-object identity, while its BiDi run fails during setup. These assertions remain intact. This PR's test link now points to the new coverage.

<details><summary>AI Feedback</summary>

Question Q1 is open.

New in this review:

Q1: In `update document for history step application`, Step 8 updates `activation` (calling `getting the navigation API entry index` on `navigation`'s `entry list`) before Step 10 calls `reactivate a document` → `update the navigation API entries for reactivation`. On contiguous same-origin BFCache restoration (`pageA` → `pageB` → back to `pageA`), `pageB`'s entry is not yet in `pageA`'s `navigation`'s `entry list` at Step 8, so `previousEntryIndex` is `-1` and 880fd03's `Otherwise` branch sets `activation`'s `old entry` (`navigation.activation.from`) to `null` per spec, while web-platform-tests/wpt#65675 subtest 1 in `navigation-api/navigation-activation/activation-bfcache.html` asserts `result.from === pageB.url`. How should we handle this?
- Option a: Keep the pre-existing spec order out of scope for #13315, file a follow-up issue in `whatwg/html`, and adjust subtest 1 in web-platform-tests/wpt#65675 so it does not fail against the current spec. Tradeoff: keeps #13315 scoped to the `activation`/`navigable` binding and `Otherwise` fallback, while leaving the spec/browser mismatch on same-origin BFCache `activation.from` for a dedicated follow-up.
- Option b: Fix the ordering in `update document for history step application` in #13315 (updating `navigation`'s `entry list` for reactivation before updating `activation`). Tradeoff: aligns the spec with Chrome and web-platform-tests/wpt#65675 subtest 1 immediately, but touches BFCache reactivation / BiDi step ordering and expands #13315's scope.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- In `update document for history step application`, Step 8 runs `getting the navigation API entry index` against `navigation`'s `entry list` before Step 10 runs `reactivate a document` → `update the navigation API entries for reactivation`.
- In `navigation-api/navigation-activation/activation-bfcache.html` (web-platform-tests/wpt#65675 at 4265f43), subtest 1 passes in Chrome by asserting `result.from === pageB.url`.
</details>

<details><summary>Previously raised items</summary>

- D1 ([comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13315#issuecomment-7133658670)): Fixed in 880fd03 and https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/commit/4265f43 (clears `activation`'s `old entry` to `null` when no previous entry is exposed, and seeds a non-null `activation.from` before cross-origin BFCache traversal in `activation-bfcache.html`).
- D2 ([comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13315#issuecomment-7133658670)): Fixed in https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/commit/4265f43 (asserts `navigation.activation === window.savedActivation` across BFCache reactivation and adds `test_navigate_existing_iframe` in `navigation_committed.py`).
</details>

Reviewed at 880fd03 on 0e292f4, with web-platform-tests/wpt#65675 at 4265f43, using spec-pr-review.
</details>
</details>

Thanks for catching this. I agree with option (a) and keeping the BFCache reactivation ordering issue separate from this PR.

I've updated web-platform-tests/wpt#65675 in f6b2580 to remove the disputed same-origin `activation.from` assertion while preserving the remaining regression coverage.

Follow-up issue filed: whatwg/html#13325. Thanks!
